# Local Router: OpenAI-Compatible Proxy Server for VS Code

This is the project-wide Product Requirements Document (PRD) and root DOX contract.

## Purpose

Point VS Code Copilot Chat, Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Codex, or scripts at `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and route to **18 built-in catalog providers** (16 static-key + 2 OAuth-subscription: Google Antigravity, GitHub Copilot) plus **any custom OpenAI-compatible API** you register—using one model namespace and one configuration UI.

### Capabilities & Topology
- **Port:** `11434` (Ollama default — drop-in). `develop` verification build uses `11436` (the main server port + 2) to avoid colliding with the running main server. Override with the `PORT` env var.
- **Model IDs:** `{provider-slug}/{presented-alias}` (e.g. `zenmux/qwen3.7-max`, `my-vendor/my-alias`) or `local-router/{router-or-fallback-id}`
- **Keys:** `/config` UI → in-memory while running → **PQC bundle** `~/.config/pqc-secrets/secrets.bundle.json` on every save (ML-KEM-768 + AES-256-GCM). Never committed to git or `providers.txt`.
- **Catalog:** `providers.txt` (16 providers, **~106** presented models in custom mode) + runtime edits in `provider-models.json` + **custom providers** in `custom-providers.json`.
- **Custom providers:** `/config` → **Add custom provider…** or `POST /api/providers` (HTTPS `/v1` upstream; loopback HTTP allowed for dev).
- **Auto-router:** `local-router/auto-router-main` — expanded curated set (`src/routing-defaults.ts`): free → subscription (`opencode-go` → Z.ai → Xiaomi) → OAuth subscription (`antigravity-gemini-3.5-flash` → `github-copilot-gemini-3.1-pro`) → paid (Wafer → ZenMux → OpenRouter → Nebius → Cline → Kilo + NIM/Modal/Zen extras); exhaustion-sorted at bootstrap; routes based on coding ability, context length, and price (includes free-tier boost; latency metrics deprecated).
- **System fallback:** `local-router/fallback-models` — **18** fixed steps (`DEFAULT_FALLBACK_ORDERED_IDS`): Ollama → NIM → Modal → Kilo/Cline free → OpenCode Zen free → OpenRouter free → **OAuth subscription (antigravity-gemini-3.5-flash at step 7, github-copilot-gemini-3.1-pro at step 8)** → Go/Z.ai/Xiaomi subscription → six paid anchors (no exhaustion re-sort on bootstrap).
- **Ollama Cloud:** Shared quota — router/fallback/pull use **nemotron-3-ultra**, **minimax-m3**, **deepseek-v4-flash** only unless a real `ollama.com` API key is set (Pro tags gated).
- **Ollama shim:** `local-router route set` → `ollama serve` starts real Ollama on `11435` and Local Router on `11434`.
- **Operator CLI:** `localrouter list`, `keys`, `router export|import|list|show|check`, `verify`, `config --open`.
- **Thinking:** Proxy toggle default **OFF** (IDE passthrough); optional levels when enabled. Responses strip `reasoning_content` for VS Code safety; requests preserve it for multi-turn tools.

```text
Clients (VS Code, Claude Code, Codex, Cline, scripts)
        │
        ▼
 127.0.0.1:11434  Local Router (Express, src/index.ts)
        │  model resolve → router / fallback / direct
        │  keys from PQC bundle + in-memory keyStore
        ▼
 Per-provider upstream OpenAI-compat APIs
        │
        └── ollama provider → 127.0.0.1:11435/v1 (real ollama serve, auto-started)
                 └── :cloud tags via local `ollama signin` session
```

### Product North Star
Local Router should become an easy local drop-in replacement for Ollama-compatible tooling: one localhost server, one familiar Ollama/OpenAI-compatible surface, and many provider-backed or locally routed models behind it.

The end-state product should feel like an approachable open-source Ollama-compatible proxy with extra routing intelligence, not a closed provider gateway. Users should be able to point VS Code, Copilot Chat, Continue, Cline, Roo Code, scripts, or Ollama-native clients at `http://127.0.0.1:11434` and keep working while Local Router handles provider keys, model aliases, fallback chains, router models, diagnostics, and explicit routing policy.

The project may take product inspiration from Ollama's local-first ergonomics and API shape, but it must remain its own implementation and brand. Do not copy Ollama source, trademarks, mascot assets, or visual identity unless a future license review explicitly permits it. Compatibility is the goal: same easy local mental model, same drop-in endpoint expectations, and clear behavior under open-source Local Router logic.

#### Visual Direction & Brand Mascot
Local Router should have a cool, cutesy cyberpunk Anishinaabe character and interface personality that makes the project memorable without weakening the operational tool surface. This character should be original, culturally respectful, and operator/community approved before it becomes a logo, mascot, generated asset, or default UI element. It should support the product as a first-viewport signal and documentation identity, while the app UI remains dense, readable, and useful for repeated routing/configuration work.

`BRAND.md` is the working source of truth for product identity and character direction. Keep it aligned with this PRD before generating or shipping visual assets.

#### Routing Direction
Auto-routing should be open, inspectable, and improvable by the community. Prefer local TypeScript/Node logic, explicit candidate lists, redacted telemetry, CSV/JSON exports, dry-run scoring, recompute tools, and documented scoring formulas over opaque hosted router behavior. Users should be able to see why a model was selected, tune the policy, share improvements, and verify that no hidden model pool or provider-managed default was used unless they configured it as a normal candidate.

### Web & Architectural Inspiration
- **Free Claude Code (`fcc-server`):** Repo: https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code — A proxy layer between Claude Code and multiple LLM backends. Local Router follows its pattern of browser UI key management and in-memory key storage.
- **Ollama:** Repo: https://github.com/ollama/ollama — Local Router mirrors Ollama's default port, HTTP route shape, and streaming response conventions so existing tools can repoint with minimal configuration.

---

## Ownership

### Codebase & Repositories
Remote: `https://github.com/nbiish/local-router.git` (`local-router` remote).
Maintained by the local-router team. Operators use the local-router agent workflow to interact with the repository.

### Branch & Integration Policy
The repository uses two long-lived branches with a mandatory two-hop promotion path:
- **`develop` — integration & verification branch.** All worktree work lands here first. This is where features integrate, build gates run, smoke tests execute, and cross-branch behavior is verified before any release promotion. `develop` is the required pre-release assembly line — not a shortcut around verification.
- **`main` — release branch.** GitHub default and production-facing canonical state. Receives only verified, fully integrated work promoted from `develop`. Full feature integration updates ship here after `develop` verification passes.

```text
feature worktree → develop (integrate + verify) → main (release)
```

#### Rules:
- Never promote feature work directly to `main`. Every change must pass through `develop` integration and verification first.
- Never commit active development on `main` or `develop`. Use isolated worktrees (`feature/*`, `docs/*`).
- Do not use `staging`, `production`, or other long-lived integration branches.
- Per `AGENTS.md`: create a git worktree for every task. One task = one branch = one worktree.
- Mandatory worktree removal and feature branch deletion is required after a `feature` -> `develop` merge.

## Local Contracts

### DOX Core Hierarchy Contract
- `llms.txt` files are binding work contracts for their subtrees.
- Work products, source materials, instructions, records, assets, and durable docs must stay understandable from the nearest applicable `llms.txt` plus every parent `llms.txt` above it.
- **Hierarchy:**
  - Root `llms.txt` is the DOX rail: project-wide instructions, global preferences, durable workflow rules, and the top-level Child DOX Index.
  - Child `llms.txt` files own domain-specific instructions and their own Child DOX Index.
  - Each parent explains what its direct children cover and what stays owned by the parent.
  - The closer a doc is to the work, the more specific and practical it must be.
- **Child Doc Shape:**
  - Create a child `llms.txt` when a folder becomes a durable boundary with its own purpose, rules, responsibilities, workflow, materials, or quality standards.
  - Default section order: Purpose, Ownership, Local Contracts, Work Guidance, Verification, Child DOX Index.

### Architecture Core Contracts
- **Runtime:** Node.js + Express + TypeScript
- **Port Invariant:** `11434` (mimicking Ollama's default for drop-in compatibility).
- **Core Upstream endpoint:** `POST /v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI format).
- **Ollama-compatible endpoints:** `GET /api/tags`, `POST /api/generate`, `POST /api/chat`, `POST /api/show`, `HEAD /api/version`, `HEAD /api/tags`, `GET /api/ps`.
- **OpenAI Responses API shim:** `POST /v1/responses` and WebSocket upgrade `ws://localhost:PORT/v1/responses` (Codex compatibility layer).
- **Anthropic Messages API proxy:** `POST /v1/messages` (Claude Code compatibility layer).
- **Discovery probes:** `GET /` and `HEAD /` return `Ollama is running`.
- **Version probe:** `GET /api/version` returns `0.6.4` to satisfy VS Code's Ollama check.
- **Upstream custom requirements:** Base URL must end with `/v1`. Vendor must support standard bearer auth and implement `POST .../chat/completions` with streaming. Mapped in `custom-providers.json` without secrets.

### PQC Key Management & Secrets Infrastructure
This is the core security system of the project. Every API key for every application — CLI tools, TUI dashboards, GUI applications, inference providers, cloud services — lives in the PQC secrets bundle. No plaintext keys are ever allowed on disk, in `.env`, or committed to git.
- **Approved Cryptographic Algorithms:** ML-KEM-768/1024 for secrets wrapping, ML-DSA-65/87 for signing/integrity, AES-256-GCM for payload encryption, Argon2id for key derivation. Classical algorithms (RSA, DSA, ECDSA, ECDH, Ed25519, AES-CBC, unauthenticated openssl) are strictly forbidden for secrets operations.
- **Infrastructure Layout:**
  - Private key: stored by default in a system-agnostic, hardware-HKDF derived file `private.key.enc` (encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a machine-bound KEK). Optionally stored in the OS Keystore (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service) when opted-in via `PQC_USE_KEYCHAIN=true`.
  - Public key: `~/.config/pqc-secrets/recipient.pub` (safe to commit).
  - Encrypted bundle: `~/.config/pqc-secrets/secrets.bundle.json` (AES-256-GCM data key wrapped with ML-KEM-768).
- **Key Resolution Order:** PQC bundle → Environment variables → Memory (saved in `/config` this session).
- **Tooling Parity:** The Python `kyber-py` script (`.agents/skills/pqc-secrets/scripts/pqc_secrets.py`) and Rust `rust-fips203` engine are fully compatible and read/pack the same bundle JSON layout.
- **Verification Signatures:** ML-DSA-65 signatures are managed via OpenSSL and the subprocess wrapper at `.agents/skills/pqc-signatures-security/scripts/pqc_helper.py`, which enforces a 30s timeout and strict returncode classification.

### Model IDs & Namespaces
Clients format model names using the patterns:
- `provider/upstream-id` (e.g. `nebius/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`) — direct upstream.
- `provider/presented-alias` (e.g. `zenmux/qwen3.7-max`) — custom or catalog friendly alias.
- `local-router/router-id` (e.g. `local-router/auto-router-main`) — candidate list auto-selection.
- `local-router/fallback-id` (e.g. `local-router/fallback-models`) — fallback ordered retry chain.

Slashes after the first segment are passed through as part of the upstream ID (e.g. OpenRouter preset paths).

### Telemetry Formats
- `router-events.csv`: Decisions logging. Columns: timestamp, router_id, presented_model, router_type, selected_model, status, duration_ms, candidate_latency_ms, stream, request features, coding_task, approx_input_tokens, requested_output_tokens, tool_calls_*, reward_signal, prompt_hash, candidate_scores, error_type. Prompt hash is SHA-256.
- `router-candidates.csv`: Candidate performance statistics. Columns: model ID, provider, upstream_model, context/output, capabilities, cost, latency, success_rate, tool_call_accuracy, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, sample_count, tier, last_observed_at.

### Configuration Directories & Settings Map
Setting files reside at `~/.config/local-router/` (or legacy `~/.config/fvs-code/` as fallback):

| File | Secret? | Persists | Purpose |
|------|---------|----------|---------|
| `secrets.bundle.json` | Encrypted | PQC pack | Mapped API keys (`WAFER_SERVERLESS_API_KEY`, etc.) |
| `recipient.pub` | No | Public | ML-KEM public key |
| `custom-providers.json` | No | local JSON | Custom provider metadata (endpoints, env variables) |
| `provider-models.json` | No | local JSON | Custom model overrides and context details |
| `router-models.json` | No | local JSON | Router specifications and candidate lists |
| `fallback-models.json` | No | local JSON | Fallback chain ordered routes |
|| `thinking-config.json` | No | local JSON | Thinking levels (none/low/medium/high/xhigh) |
|| `wafer-config.json` | No | local JSON | Wafer AI ZDR enhancement toggle (enabled by default) |
| `system-prompt.json` | No | local JSON | User system prompt injection configuration |
| `model-source-config.json` | No | local JSON | Configured source: `custom` vs `endpoints` |
| `endpoint-models-cache.json` | No | local JSON | Cached upstream `/models` query data |
| `provider-pricing.json` | No | local JSON | Cost scoring overrides |
| `sessions.json` | No | Redacted | client-grouped requests within 2-hour windows |
| `session-feedback.json` | No | Redacted | Session thumbs up/down user votes |
| `tool-routing.json` | No | local JSON | Ollama shim routing configuration |

| `antigravity` | 6 | Google Cloud Code Assist (`https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal`) | `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_TOKEN` | **oauth-pkce** |
| `github-copilot` | 5 | `https://api.githubcopilot.com` | `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | **oauth-device** |

**Auth legend:** `static` = long-lived API key in the PQC bundle. `oauth-pkce` = browser-based OAuth 2.0 authorization-code + PKCE flow. `oauth-device` = OAuth 2.0 device flow (RFC 8628).
**Note:** `antigravity` and `github-copilot` are **fully implemented** OAuth-subscription providers with active PKCE (Antigravity) and device flow (Copilot) auth, dynamic model discovery, and concurrent-refresh deduplication. Tokens persist to `~/.config/local-router/oauth-credentials.json` (chmod 600). See the "OAuth / Subscription Providers" section below for the full authentication contract, oh-my-pi design references, and integration architecture.

#### Key Model Metadata Specifications
- **1M-Context Models:** wafer-serverless (deepseek-v4-flash/pro, qwen3.7-max), zenmux (qwen3.7-max, deepseek-v4-pro), nebius (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Nemotron-3-Ultra), openrouter-presets (@preset/chain-of-draft, @preset/1-million-main/chain-of-draft), xiaomi-mimo (mimo-v2.5-pro/v2.5), minimax/minimax-m3 (all providers).
- **MiniMax M3:** 1M context, 512K output, MSA Sparse Attention architecture ($0.30/$1.20 per 1M pricing).
- **Step-3.7-flash:** 256K context, 256K output.
- **Qwen3.7-max:** 1M context, 64K output.
- **GLM-5.1:** 200K context, 128K output (Z.AI coding pass, modal FP8).
- **NVIDIA NIM Kimi K2.6:** 256K context, 262K output, multimodal image, implicit prompt cache.
- **OpenCode MiniMax M3 free tier:** 1M context, 512K output. Mapped only under `opencode-zen/minimax-m3-free`.
- **Z.ai:** `code-pass-glm-5.1` (presented model for coding GLM-5.1).

#### Prompt Caching by Provider — Read/Write Mechanics & Cost Impact
Local Router must maximize cache hits across every failover and auto-route hop. The rules below govern how `src/index.ts` (or the eventual caching module) should inject cache directives, preserve prefixes across provider transitions, and interpret cache metrics in upstream responses.

##### OpenAI (`openrouter-presets`, plus any direct OpenAI candidate)
- **Mode:** Automatic — no code changes required to enable.
- **Minimum tokens:** 1,024 tokens in the prompt prefix; first 1,024 tokens must be identical across requests. After the first 1,024, cache hits occur every 128 additional identical tokens.
- **Cache duration (in-memory):** Cached prefixes remain active for 5–10 minutes of inactivity, up to a maximum of 1 hour. Only held in volatile GPU memory. Default for gpt-4.1 and older models.
- **Cache duration (extended):** 24 hours for gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.1-family, gpt-5, gpt-5-codex, gpt-4.1. Achieved via `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`. Extended caching offloads KV tensors to GPU-local storage.
- **Cost:** Cached input tokens billed at ~50% of standard input price. Zero write premium. No additional fees for the caching feature itself.
- **Routing:** Requests are routed to a machine based on a hash of the initial prefix (first ~256 tokens). Optional `prompt_cache_key` parameter can influence routing for traffic sharing long common prefixes.
- **Latency impact:** Up to 80% reduction in time-to-first-token on cache hits.
- **Observability:** `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` returned in every response. OpenRouter additionally returns `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `audio_tokens`, and `reasoning_tokens` in the last SSE chunk.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Do not mutate the prompt prefix between turns. Place system prompts, tool definitions, and static context first; user queries last.
  - Preserve the full `messages` array (including prior assistant turns) across failover hops so the next provider can hit the same prefix.
  - When falling back from one OpenAI-compatible provider to another, note that the cache is provider-specific (not shared). The new provider starts cold, but the prefix is identical.

##### Anthropic Claude (`cline`, plus any direct Anthropic candidate via OpenRouter or Bedrock)
- **Mode:** Explicit — requires `cache_control` breakpoints on content blocks.
- **Minimum tokens:**
  - Claude Sonnet 4.6: 2,048 tokens per cacheable block.
  - Claude Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8: 4,096 tokens per cacheable block.
  - Claude Sonnet 4.5 and older: 1,024 tokens.
  - Claude Haiku 3/3.5/4.5: 1,024 tokens.
- **Cache structure:** The entire prompt prefix is cacheable: `tools` + `system` + `messages` (in that order), up to and including the block marked with `cache_control`.
- **TTL options:**
  - 5 minutes (default, since early 2026): write cost = 1.25x base input price; cache reads = 0.1x base input price.
  - 1 hour: write cost = 2x base input price; cache reads = 0.1x base input price.
  - Cache refreshes on each use at no additional cost.
- **Cost:** Cache reads are ~90% off base input price. Writes carry a 25–100% premium depending on TTL.
- **Two usage modes:**
  - **Automatic caching:** Add `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` at the top level of the request. The system applies the breakpoint to the last cacheable block and advances it as conversations grow. Best for multi-turn.
  - **Explicit breakpoints:** Place `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral", ttl: "5m" | "1h" }` directly on individual content blocks (system prompt, tool definitions, specific messages) for fine-grained control.
- **Isolation:** As of February 2026, caches are isolated per Workspace (not per Organization) on the Claude API and Azure AI Foundry. Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI retain organization-level isolation.
- **ZDR eligibility:** Prompt caching is eligible for Zero Data Retention; cached data is not stored after the response is returned.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Add `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` to the last system message and any large tool-definition blocks before forwarding to Anthropic-compatible endpoints.
  - When a failover hops from one Anthropic-backed provider to another, the new provider starts cold. Preserve the full messages array; the new provider will rebuild the cache on the next request.
  - Do not insert dynamic content (timestamps, user IDs) into cached blocks — it breaks prefix matching.

##### Google Gemini (`openrouter-presets` Gemini routes, plus any direct Gemini candidate)
- **Mode:** Two tiers — implicit (automatic) and explicit (manual).
- **Minimum tokens for implicit caching:**
  - Gemini 3.5 Flash: 1,024 tokens.
  - Gemini 3 Pro Preview: 4,096 tokens.
  - Gemini 2.5 Flash: 1,024 tokens.
  - Gemini 2.5 Pro: 4,096 tokens.
- **Minimum tokens for explicit caching:** 32,768 tokens.
- **Implicit caching:** Enabled by default on Gemini 2.5 and newer. Cost savings are passed through automatically if a cache hit occurs — no code changes needed. No cost-saving guarantee.
- **Explicit caching:** Create a `cachedContent` resource first (POST to `/v1beta/cachedContents`), then reference it by name in subsequent requests. Supports TTL control (default 1 hour if unset). Cached content can be text, images, audio, video, or PDFs.
- **Cost:** Cached reads are ~75% cheaper than fresh input for explicit caching. Implicit caching cost reduction depends on the provider (OpenRouter passes through Google's savings).
- **Observability:** `usage_metadata.cached_content_token_count` in the response.
- **OpenRouter-specific Gemini caching:** OpenRouter enables Gemini prompt caching when provider sticky routing activates. Sticky routing tracks per-account, per-model, per-conversation by hashing the first system (or developer) message and the first non-system message. Conversations sharing the same opening messages stick to the same provider.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - For direct Gemini calls, create a `cachedContent` resource on the first turn of a multi-turn conversation and reference it on subsequent turns.
  - For OpenRouter-routed Gemini calls, rely on provider sticky routing. Ensure the `messages` array is preserved verbatim across failover hops so the sticky hash remains stable.
  - Do not edit or reorder the system message once a cache is warm.

##### DeepSeek (`wafer-serverless`, `zenmux`, plus direct DeepSeek API)
- **Mode:** Automatic disk-based prefix caching. Enabled by default for all users. No code changes required.
- **Minimum tokens:** No explicit minimum published; cache builds from every request and matches on complete prefix units.
- **Cache mechanics:**
  - Each request constructs a disk cache at the end of the user input and at the end of the model output positions.
  - Common prefix detection: when multiple requests share a prefix, that prefix is extracted as an independent cache unit.
  - Fixed token-interval extraction in long inputs/outputs prevents very long prefixes from never being cached.
  - Cache is "best effort" — not 100% guaranteed.
  - Cache lifetime: typically hours to days after last use. Automatic cleanup.
- **Cost:** Cache reads are ~1/10 to 1/50 of miss price. No separate write premium — first-time tokens bill at miss price, identical prefixes on later requests bill at hit price. For deepseek-v4-flash: cache read $0.0028/M vs miss $0.14/M (50x cheaper). For deepseek-v4-pro (standard list pricing as of June 2026): cache read $0.0145/M vs miss $1.74/M (~120x cheaper). Note: the 75% limited-time V4 Pro discount expired May 31, 2026 — current list pricing applies.
- **Observability:** `usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens` and `usage.prompt_cache_miss_tokens` in every response.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - DeepSeek caching is fully automatic — no request modification needed.
  - Across failover hops, preserve the full `messages` array so the next provider (if also DeepSeek-backed) can reuse the same prefix.
  - Note: the legacy aliases `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` are scheduled for deprecation on 2026-07-24 and route to V4 Flash today. Use `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` IDs for new integrations.

##### OpenRouter (`openrouter-presets`)
- **Mode:** Provider sticky routing + pass-through of each upstream provider's caching mechanism.
- **Mechanism:**
  - After a request that uses prompt caching, OpenRouter remembers which provider served the request.
  - Subsequent requests for the same model are routed to the same provider, keeping caches warm.
  - Sticky routing activates only when the provider's cache read pricing is cheaper than regular prompt pricing.
  - If the sticky provider becomes unavailable, OpenRouter falls back to the next-best provider automatically.
  - Sticky routing is bypassed when `provider.order` is manually specified in the request.
- **Granularity:** Tracked at account level, per model, per conversation. Conversations are identified by hashing the first system (or developer) message and the first non-system message.
- **Cost:** Varies by upstream provider (see individual provider entries above). OpenRouter returns detailed usage in the last SSE chunk for streaming, or in the full response for non-streaming.
- **Usage fields (OpenRouter-specific):** `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_details.audio_tokens`, `cost`, `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` (BYOK only). Note: `usage: { include: true }` and `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` are deprecated — full usage details are now always included automatically.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - When routing through OpenRouter, do not override `provider.order` unless explicitly requested by the user — doing so breaks sticky routing.
  - Preserve message ordering and content across auto-router and fallback hops. Even a single character change in the first 1,024 tokens causes a cache miss.
  - Surface `cached_tokens` in router telemetry (`router-events.csv`) to track cache hit rates per model.

##### Moonshot / Kimi (`moonshot`, plus any Kimi route via OpenRouter or Groq)
- **Mode:** Two mechanisms depending on model series:
  - **K2 series (kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6):** Automatic prefix caching — no code changes required. 50% discount on cached tokens. Requires exact prefix preservation; the model's `reasoning_content` from prior responses must be included verbatim or the cache is invalidated. Optional `prompt_cache_key` request field for sticky routing to ensure repeated requests hit the same cache server.
  - **moonshot-v1 (legacy):** Explicit context caching via `/v1/caching` API with `role: cache` + `cache_id` reference.
- **K2 series cost:** Cached input tokens at ~50% discount (e.g. cache hit $0.20/M vs miss $0.40/M for kimi-k2.6). Zero write premium.
- **K2 series cache persistence:** Prefix cache survives across multi-turn conversations as long as the identical prefix (including prior `reasoning_content`) is preserved.
- **Legacy moonshot-v1 cost:** ~75% discount on cached tokens. Requires explicit cache lifecycle management.
- **Context window:** Kimi K2.5/K2.6 support 256K context. The cache covers the full prefix within that window.
- **Observability:** Token usage via `/api/estimate`; K2 series returns standard `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.
- **Invalidation rules (both mechanisms):** Invalidate when system prompt changes, tool definitions/schema change, model changes, or the provider returns "unknown/expired" reference. For K2 series, any edit/reorder to prior messages (including removal of `reasoning_content`) invalidates the cache.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - For K2 series, preserve the full `messages` array verbatim — including assistant `reasoning_content` fields — across turns and failover hops.
  - Use `prompt_cache_key` with a stable session-derived value when routing K2 series traffic to maximize sticky routing to a single cache server.
  - For legacy moonshot-v1, store `context_id` per session in `sessions.json`. Invalidate on any prefix change.
  - On provider failover, cache state is provider-specific. Start fresh on the new provider but preserve the full messages array.

##### Groq (Kimi K2-Instruct route, GPT-OSS models via `openrouter-presets` or direct)
- **Mode:** Automatic prefix matching — no code changes required.
- **Minimum tokens:** No explicit minimum published; prefix matching works across all request sizes, but cache hits require sufficient shared prefix length.
- **Cache mechanics:**
  - Prefix Matching: The system identifies matching prefixes from recently processed requests stored in volatile memory (in-RAM only).
  - Cache Hit: Cached computation is reused. Cached input tokens receive 50% discount. Latency is significantly reduced.
  - Cache Miss: Prompt processed normally; prefix cached for potential future matches.
  - Automatic Expiration: All cached data expires after 2 hours of inactivity.
- **Supported models (as of June 2026):**
  - `moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct`: $1.00/M uncached, $0.50/M cached, $3.00/M output.
  - `openai/gpt-oss-20b`: $0.075/M uncached, $0.0375/M cached.
  - `openai/gpt-oss-120b`: $0.15/M uncached, $0.075/M cached.
- **Rate limits:** Cached tokens do not count toward rate limits (they are subtracted from limits after processing, so parallel large requests can still hit limits).
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Groq caching is fully automatic — no request modification needed.
  - Place static content (system prompts, tool definitions, few-shot examples) at the beginning of the prompt and dynamic content (user queries, timestamps) at the end to maximize prefix match length.
  - Preserve the full messages array across failover hops within the same Groq provider. Note: failover to a non-Groq provider loses the cache.

##### NVIDIA NIM (`nvidia-nim`)
- **Mode (hosted API):** No prompt caching on the NVIDIA-hosted API endpoint (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`). Full prefill on every request.
- **Mode (self-hosted deployment):** KV cache reuse available via `NIM_ENABLE_KV_CACHE_REUSE=1` or `--enable-prefix-caching` flag (TRT-LLM backend). Host memory offloading via `NIM_ENABLE_KV_CACHE_HOST_OFFLOAD` with `NIM_KV_CACHE_HOST_MEM_FRACTION` (default 0.1). ~2x TTFT speedup for repeated prefixes. No HTTP-level caching API — purely deployment-level configuration via environment variables or CLI flags.
- **Model weight caching:** NIM's `/opt/nim/.cache` (or `NIM_CACHE_PATH`) is for model weight storage between container restarts, not for prefix caching across inference requests. Requires persistent volume mounts (`-v ~/.cache/nim:/opt/nim/.cache`) in Kubernetes or Docker.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Do not inject cache directives for the hosted NIM API — it does not support prompt caching.
  - For self-hosted NIM deployments behind Local Router, KV cache reuse is handled entirely at the deployment level. No request-level changes needed.
  - When failover reaches NIM (hosted), the model cold-starts with a full prefill.

##### Xiaomi MiMo (`xiaomi-mimo`, plus any MiMo route via ZenMux or OpenRouter)
- **Mode:** Automatic server-side prompt caching. Enabled by default. No code changes required.
- **Cache architecture:** Dual-pool KVCache with SWA-aware prefix cache trees. GCache distributed cache system spans multiple servers with slot-based hash mapping. Engineering blog reports 93–95% server-side cache hit rate in production.
- **Minimum tokens:** No explicit minimum published; cache builds from every request and matches on shared prefixes.
- **Cost:** ~99% discount on cache hits. Token Plan pricing (mimo-v2.5-pro): cache hit 2.5 credits vs miss 300 credits. Cache write at miss price (no write premium).
- **Observability:** Standard `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in responses.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Fully automatic — no request modification needed. Place static system prompts and tool definitions first; dynamic content last to maximize prefix match.
  - Preserve the full `messages` array across failover hops within the same MiMo-backed provider.

##### Z.ai / GLM (`zai`, plus any GLM route via ZenMux, Modal, Nebius, or OpenRouter)
- **Mode:** Automatic context caching (implicit). Enabled by default on all GLM-4.5 through GLM-5.1 models. No code changes required.
- **Cache mechanics:**
  - Server-side prefix matching across consecutive requests. No manual `cache_control` directives needed.
  - "Preserved Thinking" mode (`clear_thinking: false`) increases cache hit rates by keeping reasoning KV state warm across turns.
- **Minimum tokens:** No explicit minimum published; cache builds from shared prefixes across requests.
- **Cost:** Cache hits at reduced pricing (specific multiplier not published by Z.ai as of June 2026). Implicit — savings are pass-through.
- **Observability:** `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in every response.
- **Implementation guidance for Local Router:**
  - Fully automatic — no request modification needed.
  - For GLM-5.1 with reasoning enabled, preserve `reasoning_content` in assistant messages to maintain cache warmth across turns.
  - When GLM-5.1 is routed via Modal, Nebius, or other pass-through providers, caching depends on the intermediate layer. Direct Z.ai or ZenMux routes preserve caching.

##### Providers Without Prompt Caching Support
- **Nebius:** No prompt caching support. Full prefill on every request.
- **Modal:** Infrastructure platform (not a model provider). Runs vLLM/SGLang underneath. GPU memory snapshots for fast cold starts. No native prompt caching of its own; caching depends on the deployed inference engine (vLLM's `--enable-prefix-caching` available for self-hosted Modal deployments, but the Modal GLM endpoint does not expose or enable it). Full prefill on every request through the hosted endpoint.
- **Wafer Serverless:** No documented prompt caching support (passes through to upstream; caching depends on upstream provider, typically DeepSeek which handles it automatically).
- **Ollama local (`ollama` provider, port 11435):** No prompt caching across requests. Each request to the local Ollama backend processes from scratch.
- **CommandCode:** No documented prompt caching support.

##### Cross-Provider Failover Caching Contract
When Local Router fails over from provider A to provider B:
1. **Prefix preservation:** The full `messages` array (system + all prior turns) MUST be forwarded unchanged so provider B can apply its own caching logic from an identical prefix.
2. **Cache isolation:** No cache state transfers between providers. Provider B starts cold, but the identical prefix means its own cache will rebuild on the first request and hit on the second.
3. **Telemetry continuity:** Record `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and `error_type` in `router-events.csv` for every request regardless of provider. This enables cache hit rate analysis across the full fallback chain.
4. **Cost tracking:** Surface provider-specific usage fields (`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`) in a normalized form in telemetry so operators can compare effective costs across providers.
5. **Tool definitions:** Tool definitions are part of the cacheable prefix for OpenAI and Anthropic. Do not reorder, rename, or restructure tool definitions between turns — even a single character change invalidates the cache.

### Ollama Intercept Shim Contracts
`local-router route set` installs a shim at `~/.local/bin/ollama` (first in PATH) that intercepts `ollama serve`:
1. Sets `OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435`.
2. Starts real Ollama on port `11435` in the background.
3. Sets `LOCAL_ROUTER_PROVIDER_OLLAMA_BASE_URL` to local server.
4. Starts Local Router on `11434` in the foreground.
5. Other commands (pull, run, show) pass through directly to real `/usr/local/bin/ollama`.
6. Marker comment line: `# local-router ollama shim`.
7. Trap cleans up the real Ollama process PID on exit.

### OpenAI Responses API Shim Contract
- Maps Responses requests (`POST /v1/responses`) to standard chat-completion payloads (prepends `instructions` as system prompt).
- Executes normal routing and returns the re-wrapped responses payload envelope (`object: "response"`, `output` array of parts).
- HTTP SSE is mapped via a shared translator (`src/responses-stream.ts`) which also services WebSocket upgrade connections at `ws://localhost:PORT/v1/responses`.

### Anthropic Messages API Proxy Contract
- Translates Anthropic requests (`POST /v1/messages`) to OpenAI shape.
- Maps non-streaming completions to Anthropic `message` structures.
- Stream handler converts standard SSE to Anthropic events: `message_start`, `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`.

### User Preferences
When the user requests a durable behavior change, record it here or in the relevant child `llms.txt`.
- CoD prompt injection is disabled by default.
- Global thinking/reasoning default is `none` for VS Code safety.

---

## Work Guidance

### DOX Framework Workflow Rules

#### Read Before Editing
1. Read the root `llms.txt`.
2. Identify every file or folder you expect to touch.
3. Walk from the repository root to each target path.
4. Read every `llms.txt` found along each route.
5. If a parent `llms.txt` lists a child `llms.txt` whose scope contains the path, read that child and continue from there.
6. Use the nearest `llms.txt` as the local contract and parent docs for repo-wide rules.
7. If docs conflict, the closer doc controls local work details, but no child doc may weaken DOX.
Do not rely on memory. Re-read the applicable DOX chain in the current session before editing.

#### Update After Editing
Every meaningful change requires a DOX pass before the task is done.
Update the closest owning `llms.txt` when a change affects:
- purpose, scope, ownership, or responsibilities
- durable structure, contracts, workflows, or operating rules
- required inputs, outputs, permissions, constraints, side effects, or artifacts
- user preferences about behavior, communication, process, organization, or quality
- `llms.txt` creation, deletion, move, rename, or index contents
Update parent docs when parent-level structure, ownership, workflow, or child index changes. Update child docs when parent changes alter local rules. Remove stale or contradictory text immediately. Small edits that do not change behavior or contracts may leave docs unchanged, but the DOX pass still must happen.

#### Style
- Keep docs concise, current, and operational.
- Document stable contracts, not diary entries.
- Put broad rules in parent docs and concrete details in child docs.
- Prefer direct bullets with explicit names.
- Do not duplicate rules across many files unless each scope needs a local version.
- Delete stale notes instead of explaining history.
- Trim obvious statements, repeated rules, misplaced detail, and warnings for risks that no longer exist.

### Routing Logic Guidance

#### Routing Exhaustion Sequence
`stableSortModelIdsByRoutingExhaustion()` orders candidate models and custom fallback routes:
**Free (1-4) → Subscription (5) → Paid (6)**

1. `ollama` free-tier `:cloud` tags (only 3 allowed: nemotron-3-ultra, minimax-m3, deepseek-v4-flash).
2. `kilo` free gateway (curated to Nemotron Ultra + Step 3.7 Flash only).
3. `cline` free gateway (curated to Nemotron Ultra + MiniMax M3 only).
4. Other free models (e.g. `openrouter/free`, `opencode-zen-*-free`).
5. **Subscription band:** `opencode-go` → `zai` → `xiaomi-mimo` → `commandcode`.
6. **Paid API order:** `wafer-serverless` → `zenmux` → `openrouter-presets` → `nebius` → `cline` → `kilo` → `opencode-zen` → `nvidia-nim` → `modal`.
   - **Fallback paid tail (fixed seven):** `wafer-ai-deepseek-v4-flash` → `zenmux-mimo-v2.5-pro` → `openrouter-chain-of-draft` → `nebius-nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` → `cline-deepseek-deepseek-v4-flash-free` → `kilo-deepseek-deepseek-v4-flash-paid` → `commandcode-deepseek-v4-pro`.

#### Candidate Selection & Execution Plan
- `selectRouterCandidate()` chooses the **first eligible** model in the sorted exhaustion list. Eligibility checks fail if keys are missing or provider cloud tags are blocked.
- `buildWraparoundExecutionPlan()` implements retries. Before advancing to next candidate `N+1`, the plan bridges back to retrying earlier candidates `0...N` once to allow for rate-limit/quota recovery window (e.g. subscription buckets reset).
- Direct chat failures from gateway providers (Cline/Kilo) return errors immediately without cascading to fallback routes.

#### Fallback Stages & Skip Preflight
- Fallback route `fallback-models` follows a fixed 18-step bootstrap order. Legacy configurations might use the `default` alias.
- Normal fallback execution runs 3 attempts per stage using `{baseSeconds}^retryIndex` wait logic (2s base).
- Stages with missing keys or blocked Ollama clouds are skipped instantly during fallback preflight checks.

#### Ollama Cloud Gating (Free vs Pro)
Ollama Cloud uses a shared quota. Free cloud tags use `ollama signin` session key (`local-router-ollama`), whereas Pro-only tags are skipped unless a real `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is present.
- Curated Free: `nemotron-3-ultra:cloud`, `minimax-m3:cloud`, `deepseek-v4-flash:cloud`.
- Pro-Only (gated): `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud`, `kimi-k2.6:cloud`, `glm-5.1:cloud`, `qwen3.5:cloud`, `minimax-m2.7:cloud`.
- persisted routes are run through `pruneDisallowedOllamaCloudRouting()` on start to remove unauthorized Pro tags.

#### Cline & Kilo Gateway Allowlisting
- **Cline:** Custom catalog is strictly limited to 4 free + 8 paid chat-proven models. Standard vendors (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI) are excluded.
- **Kilo:** Custom catalog is limited to 8 free + 11 paid models. `kilo-auto/free` is excluded.
- Custom catalogs represent the baseline `providers.txt` models. To search all upstream gateway models, Endpoint Models mode must be enabled with live fetch toggles.

### Operator UI, CLI & Configuration

#### Setup and Configuration
1. **First-run:** Copy `.env.example` as `.env` (optional fallback for development, do not save keys here).
2. **Setup keys:** Open `/config` UI or run `localrouter keys set`. Mapped keys will encrypt at rest using the PQC bundle automatically. Mappings are deduplicated (e.g., `OPENCODE_API_KEY` shared across `opencode-go` and `opencode-zen`).
3. **Configure clients:** Repoint client base URL to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` (OpenAI compatible) or `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (Ollama) and select the desired model.

#### CLI Reference Cheat Sheet
```bash
local-router start|stop|status                      # daemon lifecycle
local-router route set|unset|custom|status           # Ollama serve shim settings
localrouter list --custom                            # lists custom catalog (providers.txt)
localrouter list --all                               # lists catalog + endpoint cache
localrouter keys list|set|unset                      # key management via PQC endpoints
localrouter router list|show|check                   # router configuration check
localrouter router export|import <file>              # routing state backup (CI/CD)
localrouter verify --json                            # headless verification check
localrouter config --open                            # launch browser config page
```

#### Configuration UI Pages API
- `GET /api/provider-configs` — merged custom and catalog provider states.
- `POST /api/providers` — register custom OpenAI-compatible provider metadata.
- `GET /api/provider-models` — retrieve full catalog model data.
- `POST /api/refresh-endpoint-models` — live upstream fetch of `/models` (6s timeout).
- `GET /api/thinking-level` / `PUT /api/thinking-level` — configuration of thinking levels.
- `GET /api/wafer-config` / `PUT /api/wafer-config` — Wafer AI ZDR enhancement toggle (enabled by default).
- `GET /api/system-prompt` / `PUT /api/system-prompt` — system prompt configuration.
- `GET /api/sessions` / `POST /api/sessions/:id/feedback` — session viewer and feedback.

#### Troubleshooting
- **Model unknown / 400 provider not found:** check `localrouter list` output. Confirm the presented slug exists. Check for spelling.
- **Auto-router skips all candidates:** Check logs for `[PQC] Providers without keys`. Configure at least one candidate provider key.
- **Ollama cloud models missing:** Ensure `ollama signin` session is active. Confirm `[ollama] Backend ready` in server logs.
- **Restart loop / CLI issues:** Check logs at `~/.config/local-router/proxy-11434.log` (or `~/.config/fvs-code/`). Verify no duplicate servers listen on port 11434.

### Reasoning & Thinking Layer
VS Code Copilot Chat strips reasoning tags on follow-up requests, leading to upstream API failures (e.g. Moonshot throws because prior assistant messages are missing reasoning metadata).
- **Request Sanitization:** `sanitizeProviderRequestBody` does not strip `reasoning_content` from request history. It only maps the thinking level parameters. Ollama-only `think` blocks are removed before forwarding.
- **Response Sanitization:** Strips reasoning metadata from final non-streaming OpenAI-compatible responses, OpenAI SSE chunks, and skips empty reasoning-only chunks in Ollama stream translations to prevent blank assistant chunks in the IDE.
- **Levels:** `none` (default), `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`.
  - OpenAI-style: `reasoning_effort: "low" | "medium" | "high"`.
  - DeepSeek/Qwen/GLM/Kimi/Step/MiniMax: `enable_thinking: true`.
  - Level `none` injects disable hints (`reasoning_effort: "none"`, `thinking: { type: "disabled" }`).
- **Configuration Grid:** Controlled per-provider in `/config` or via `PUT /api/thinking-level`; saved to `thinking-config.json`.

### Wafer AI ZDR Enhancement Toggle
- **Provider:** `wafer-serverless` only.
- **Eligible models:** `GLM-5.1`, `Kimi-K2.6`.
- **Header:** `Wafer-ZDR: required` injected on eligible models when toggle is on.
- **Default:** ON (enabled) — ZDR is a free inference enhancement.
- **Persistence:** `~/.config/local-router/wafer-config.json`.
- **Toggle location:** `/config` UI under Wafer AI provider card, or via `PUT /api/wafer-config`.

### Custom System Prompt Injection
- **Default:** OFF (disabled).
- **Default prompt:** Chain of Draft reasoning style — *"Think step by step, but only keep a minimum draft for each thinking step, with 5 words at most. Return the answer after your thinking."*
- **Persistence:** `~/.config/local-router/system-prompt.json`.
- Injection prepends `{ role: "system", content: "<prompt>" }` at the head of the messages array prior to forwarding. Compatible with reasoning sanitization.

### VS Code & Ollama Metadata
- **VS Code target:** 1.113+, Copilot Chat 0.41.0+, Ollama 0.18.3+.
- **Ollama compat:** `/api/tags` / `POST /api/show` return standard alias mappings (`basename`, `name`, `details.parameter_size`). Capabilities are advertised (`completion`, `tools`, `vision`). `thinking` is omitted.
- **Integration API:** `POST /api/vscode/configure` modifies `chatLanguageModels.json` and updates `globalStorage/state.vscdb` to insert custom presented aliases and capabilities.

### Router & Bandit Models
Presented as `local-router/<router-name>` (saved to `router-models.json`):
- **Pareto-code:** uses `minCodingScore` filters, cost/latency tie-breakers.
- **Auto-local:** uses task features (tool use, image, context size, cache, prior success/latency).
- **Bandit-local:** dLinUCB with discount forgetting factor `γ=0.98`, UCB selection (`explorationBudget` UCB coefficient), persisted matrices.
- **System fallback:** `fallback-models` safety net.

#### Statistical Outlier Tiering (Auto Exacto)
- Uses median and Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) over accumulated telemetry.
- Models categorized into: `verified` (50+ samples within threshold), `insufficient` (<50 samples), and `deranked` (outliers or success rate < 0.85).
- Recomputed via `POST /api/router-models/:id/recompute` which reads telemetry and offers tier change proposals. Mapped to `enableAutoTiers` flag in router settings.

### CIP Telemetry System
- **cip-daily-research.mts:** Computes metrics (insufficient data, deranked models, latency warnings) from CSV logs, appends findings to `cip-findings.jsonl`.
- **cip-apply-findings.mts:** Reads findings and patches `router-models.json` settings automatically.
- **crx-validate.mts:** Schema check on community registry pull requests.
- **crx-aggregate.mts:** consensus merging script (majority vote, high-consensus filters).

### Roadmap / Next Steps
- **Config UI Modularization:** Extract the inline HTML/JS config routes (~3400 lines) from `src/index.ts` into TS route modules (`src/routes/config-*.ts`), mapping shared memory to a consolidated `ConfigState` object.
- **Scoring Normalization:** Normalize scoring to `[0,1]` and map weights derived dynamically from `costQualityTradeoff`.
- **Complexity Vectors:** Add `codeDensity`, `languageCount`, `multiTurnDepth`, and `instructionLength` to auto-router scoring logic.
- **Bandit Management:** Implement UCB state export/import endpoints for backup/restore.

- **2026-06-11:** Fixed CLI `local-router stop` failing with stale PID. Root cause: `cmdStop` only SIGTERM'd the PID recorded in `proxy-state.json`; when the server was started via `tsx watch` or the PID was stale, the actual node process listening on 11434 was a different PID (child of tsx). Added `findPidsOnPort()` (lsof-based port PID discovery), `killProcessTree()` (process group SIGTERM to catch tsx/npm parent+child trees), and 3-phase shutdown in `cmdStop`: (1) process-group kill of recorded PID, (2) after 5 failed probes lsof discovers port PIDs and kills trees, (3) final SIGKILL via lsof as last resort. `local-router stop && local-router start` verified working end-to-end. Merged `fix/cli-stop-start` → `develop` → `main`.

- **2026-06-11:** Remediated hardcoded OAuth secrets. `src/oauth-providers.ts` had `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID` and `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` as string literals on lines 72-73. GitHub push protection correctly flagged them. Moved both to `process.env` reads; packed values into the PQC secrets bundle at `~/.config/pqc-secrets/secrets.bundle.json` alongside all other API keys. Updated `providers.txt` to document the new env vars. Redacted historical secret references from `llms.txt` session log. Merged `fix/oauth-secrets-env` → `develop` → `main`.

## Provider Integration Research — OAuth / Subscription Providers (June 2026)

Research into integrating two new provider types that use OAuth authentication instead of static API keys: **Google Antigravity** and **GitHub Copilot**. These are subscription-based providers with quota-limited access. The goal is to add them as first-class providers in the Local Router catalog alongside the existing 15 static-key providers.

### Why These Providers

Both Antigravity and GitHub Copilot offer access to frontier models (Claude, GPT, Gemini) through a single subscription, making them high-value additions to the Local Router provider catalog. Unlike current providers that use static API keys, these require OAuth flows with short-lived tokens and automatic refresh.

### Provider 1: Google Antigravity (Subscription / Quota-Limited)

**Product Overview:**
- Google Antigravity is an agent-based AI development platform launched November 2025 (VS Code-based, built by the ex-Windsurf team acquired for $2.4B).
- At Google I/O May 2026, it expanded to a five-surface platform: Antigravity 2.0 (desktop), Antigravity CLI (`agy`), Antigravity SDK, Managed Agents API, and Enterprise.
- Replaced Gemini CLI (shutdown June 18, 2026). CLI binary is Go-based, invoked as `agy`.
- Built-in models: Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-OSS 120B.
- Pricing: Free ($0, 20 req/day, Gemini Flash only), AI Pro ($20/mo, 1,000 credits), AI Ultra ($250/mo, 25,000 credits).
- Uses a hybrid quota system: sprint quota (5-hour refresh) + weekly baseline cap + AI credits for overage.

**Authentication Flow — OAuth 2.0 with PKCE:**
1. Client generates PKCE verifier/challenge pair (SHA-256 + base64url).
2. Opens browser to Google OAuth authorization URL: `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`
3. Required OAuth scopes: `cloud-platform`, `userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`, `cclog`, `experimentsandconfigs`
4. Redirect URI: local HTTP server (e.g. `http://localhost:51121/oauth-callback`) or manual paste for headless.
5. Exchange authorization code for tokens at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` (includes `client_id`, `client_secret`, PKCE `code_verifier`).
6. Access token + refresh token returned. Access token is short-lived; refresh token is long-lived.
7. Auto-refresh: when access token expires, use refresh token to get a new one at the same token endpoint.

**API Surface:**
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions format.
- Model discovery via API (dynamic model list).
- Streaming SSE support.
- Usage/quota tracking via response headers or separate API.
- Version override available: `PI_AI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION` env var.

**Implementation Notes for Local Router:**
- Provider ID: `antigravity` (slug).
- Key env var: `ANTIGRAVITY_OAUTH_TOKEN` (but token is short-lived, needs refresh).
- The token lifecycle management is fundamentally different from static-key providers. The Local Router key store (`keyStore`) currently assumes static strings. We need a new `OAuthProviderState` that stores `{ accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt }` per provider and a background refresh timer.
- The `/config` UI needs an "OAuth Login" button (opens browser to Google auth flow) instead of a text field for API key entry.
- The `POST /api/keys` endpoint needs a new branch for OAuth providers that stores the initial token set instead of a plain API key.
- New module needed: `src/oauth-providers.ts` — handles PKCE generation, local callback server, token exchange, auto-refresh, and credential persistence.
- The PQC bundle must store OAuth tokens (access + refresh + expiry) alongside static API keys. The existing `secrets.bundle.json` format can be extended with a per-provider `authType: 'oauth' | 'static'` discriminator.
- Quota awareness: Antigravity has strict quota limits. The Local Router routing logic should be extended to track quota exhaustion per-provider (detect 429 responses or quota-specific error codes) and temporarily deprioritize or skip the provider.

**Reference Implementations:**
- `oh-my-pi` / `pi-mono` (upstream): `npx @mariozechner/pi-ai login google-antigravity` — full OAuth PKCE flow with `loginAntigravity()` function. Uses `auth.json` for credential persistence. Auto-refresh via `getOAuthApiKey('google-antigravity', auth)`. ([mintlify.wiki/badlogic/pi-mono/ai/oauth](https://mintlify.wiki/badlogic/pi-mono/ai/oauth))
- `opencode-google-antigravity-auth` plugin: PKCE flow, multi-account load balancing (up to 10 Google accounts), automatic rate-limit detection and account switching, streaming response transformation, thinking block extraction. ([deepwiki.com/shekohex/opencode-google-antigravity-auth](https://deepwiki.com/shekohex/opencode-google-antigravity-auth/6.3-api-endpoints-and-constants))
- PicoClaw: Complete Antigravity auth guide with PKCE implementation, token management, model fetching, usage tracking. ([docs.picoclaw.io/docs/providers/antigravity](https://docs.picoclaw.io/docs/providers/antigravity/))
- `oh-my-opencode` / `fractalmind-ai`: Internal auth component integrating with `opencode-antigravity-auth` plugin for multi-account Gemini access. ([deepwiki.com/fractalmind-ai/oh-my-opencode/8.6-google-antigravity-authentication](https://deepwiki.com/fractalmind-ai/oh-my-opencode/8.6-google-antigravity-authentication))

### Provider 2: GitHub Copilot (Subscription / Quota-Limited)

**Product Overview:**
- GitHub Copilot exposes a standard OpenAI-style endpoint at `https://api.githubcopilot.com`.
- Subscription includes access to multiple frontier models: Claude (Sonnet, Opus), GPT (4o, 4.1, 5.x), Gemini, o-series — all through a single API.
- Copilot CLI provides `copilot login` — OAuth device flow authentication.
- Tokens are short-lived (~30 minutes). Must be refreshed by re-exchanging the GitHub OAuth token for a new Copilot API token.

**Authentication Flow — OAuth Device Flow (RFC 8628):**
1. CLI requests device code from `https://github.com/login/device/code` (well-known public Copilot client ID: `Iv1.b507a08c87ecfe98`).
2. User visits `https://github.com/login/device` and enters the short code displayed in the terminal.
3. CLI polls `https://github.com/github/login/oauth/access_token` until the user authorizes.
4. GitHub token (`ghu_...` or `gho_...`) is exchanged for a short-lived Copilot API token via `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` with `Authorization: token <github_token>`.
5. Response: `{ "token": "tid=...", "expires_at": "..." }`.
6. The Copilot API token (~30 min lifetime) is used as bearer auth for all API calls.
7. When expired, re-exchange the stored GitHub token for a fresh Copilot API token.

**Required Runtime Headers:**
```
Authorization: Bearer <copilot_api_token>
Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat
Editor-Version: vscode/1.99.0
Editor-Plugin-Version: copilot-chat/0.26.7
User-Agent: GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7
openai-intent: conversation-panel
x-github-api-version: 2025-04-01
```

**API Surface:**
- Base URL: `https://api.githubcopilot.com` (OpenAI-compatible).
- Model discovery: `GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models` — returns dynamic model list based on subscription entitlement.
- Chat completions: `POST /chat/completions` (standard OpenAI format for most models).
- Claude-family models: route to `/v1/messages` (Anthropic format). Must strip `cache_control.ephemeral.scope` — Copilot rejects this Claude API extension field.
- GPT-5 Responses-capable models: route to `/responses` (except `gpt-5-mini` which stays on chat completions).
- Streaming SSE support.

**Implementation Notes for Local Router:**
- Provider ID: `github-copilot` (slug).
- Key env var: `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (the long-lived GitHub OAuth token, not the short-lived API token).
- Same OAuth token lifecycle challenge as Antigravity — needs `OAuthProviderState` with `{ githubToken, copilotApiToken, copilotApiTokenExpires }`.
- The `/config` UI needs a "Login with GitHub" device-flow button instead of a key text field.
- The Copilot device flow is simpler than Antigravity PKCE — no browser callback server needed, just terminal-based code entry. However, it has the extra step of exchanging the GitHub token for a Copilot API token.
- Important: The `Copilot-Integration-Id: vscode-chat` header is **required** on all API requests. Without it, GitHub returns `400 model_not_available_for_integrator: copilot-language-server` for newer models. This was a significant bug discovered and fixed in oh-my-pi PR #1210.
- Model routing logic needs to handle the split between `/chat/completions` (most models), `/v1/messages` (Claude models), and `/responses` (GPT-5 models) — currently Local Router only uses `/chat/completions` for all providers.
- The existing `custom-providers.json` cannot express these provider-specific routing rules. We may need a new `auth-providers.json` schema or extend `providers.txt` with auth type metadata.
- Credential dedup: oh-my-pi discovered that repeated logins accumulate duplicate credential rows because `ghu_`/`gho_` tokens are opaque (not JWTs). Fix: call `GET /api.github.com/user` after device flow to get the stable numeric GitHub user ID, use it as `accountId` for dedup. Local Router should implement this pattern from the start.
- Token storage: JetBrains IDEs store the Copilot OAuth token at `~/.config/github-copilot/apps.json`. We could optionally read this file for initial token discovery.

**Reference Implementations:**
- `oh-my-pi` / `pi-mono`: `npx @mariozechner/pi-ai login github-copilot` — full device flow with `loginGitHubCopilot()` function. PR #1210 added `Copilot-Integration-Id` header and credential dedup via `GET /api.github.com/user`. ([github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/1210](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/1210))
- Aider: Direct REST endpoint usage — set `OPENAI_API_BASE=https://api.githubcopilot.com` + `OPENAI_API_KEY=<oauth_token>`. Reads token from `~/.config/github-copilot/apps.json`. ([aider.chat/docs/llms/github.html](https://aider.chat/docs/llms/github.html))
- Conduit (Icehunter): Wire contract documented in `PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md`. Covers device-code auth, token exchange, model discovery, runtime headers, Claude-family `/v1/messages` routing, and GPT-5 `/responses` routing. ([github.com/Icehunter/conduit/blob/main/PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/Icehunter/conduit/blob/main/PROVIDER_COMPATIBILITY.md))
- LiteLLM: Full Copilot provider with authenticator, model information, and test suite. ([litellm docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/github_copilot))
- byterover-cli: Feature request #322 with detailed technical design for Copilot as first-class provider, including device flow, model discovery, provider registry entry, and scope of changes. ([github.com/campfirein/byterover-cli/issues/322](https://github.com/campfirein/byterover-cli/issues/322))
- forgiven: ADR 0004 documenting both LSP-side auth (device flow via `copilot-language-server`) and HTTP-side auth (agent panel token lifecycle with auto-refresh 60s before expiry). ([github.com/daneb/forgiven/blob/master/docs/adr/0004-copilot-authentication.md](https://github.com/daneb/forgiven/blob/master/docs/adr/0004-copilot-authentication.md))

### Shared Implementation Architecture

Both providers share a common challenge: **OAuth token lifecycle management** in a system currently designed for static API keys. The implementation plan:

1. **New TypeScript module: `src/oauth-providers.ts`**
   - `OAuthProviderState` interface: `{ provider: string, authType: 'oauth-pkce' | 'oauth-device', accessToken: string, refreshToken: string, expiresAt: number, accountId?: string }`
   - `loginAntigravity()` — PKCE flow: generate verifier/challenge, open browser, local callback server, token exchange.
   - `loginGitHubCopilot()` — Device flow: request device code, display code + URL, poll until authorized, exchange for Copilot API token, call `GET /api.github.com/user` for dedup.
   - `refreshOAuthToken(provider)` — Auto-refresh access tokens before expiry. For Copilot: re-exchange GitHub token for new API token. For Antigravity: use refresh token at Google OAuth endpoint.
   - `getOAuthApiKey(provider)` — Returns current valid access token, triggering refresh if needed. Drop-in replacement for `keyStore[provider]` reads.
   - Background refresh timer (check every 60s, refresh 5 minutes before expiry).

2. **PQC Bundle Extension**
   - Extend `secrets.bundle.json` payload to support `authType: 'oauth'` entries alongside existing static key entries.
   - OAuth entries store `{ authType, accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, accountId }` — all encrypted via AES-256-GCM + ML-KEM-768 as today.
   - The `pqc-secrets pack` / `pqc-secrets export` tools should be updated to handle OAuth entries, or the tokens should be managed entirely within the Local Router's own encrypted storage.

3. **Config UI Extension**
   - New "Login with..." buttons for OAuth providers (opens browser / displays device code).
   - Visual token status indicator (green = valid, yellow = expiring, red = expired, grey = not configured).
   - Quota usage display for Antigravity (if API provides it).

4. **Routing Integration**
   - New exhaustion tier: **Subscription OAuth** (between existing Subscription band and Paid band).
   - Quota-aware routing: detect 429 / quota-exhausted responses, temporarily deprioritize the provider.
   - The `providers.txt` catalog needs new metadata fields: `auth_type`, `oauth_provider`, `required_headers`.
   - New `providers.txt` entries:
     ```
     antigravity         | https://antigravity.googleapis.com/v1    | ANTAGRAVITY_OAUTH_TOKEN | oauth-pkce
     github-copilot      | https://api.githubcopilot.com            | COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN    | oauth-device
     ```

5. **Files to Create or Modify**
   - New: `src/oauth-providers.ts` — OAuth flows, token management, refresh logic.
   - New: `src/oauth-callback-server.ts` — Temporary HTTP server for PKCE callback (Antigravity).
   - New: `tests/oauth-providers.test.mjs` — Test suite for OAuth flows (mocked).
   - Modify: `src/index.ts` — Wire OAuth provider state into key resolution, add `/api/oauth/login/:provider` and `/api/oauth/status/:provider` endpoints.
   - Modify: `src/routes/config-api.ts` — OAuth login button handling, token status display.
   - Modify: `providers.txt` — Add `antigravity` and `github-copilot` provider entries with auth type metadata.
   - Modify: `src/routing-defaults.ts` — Add OAuth provider models to auto-router candidate lists.
   - Modify: `src/key-management.ts` — Extend key store to handle OAuth token state alongside static keys.
   - Modify: `src/ui/pages/providers.ts` — OAuth login UI components.
   - Modify: PQC secrets handling — Support `authType` discriminator in bundle payload.

---

## Child DOX Index

- [src/llms.txt](src/llms.txt) — TypeScript source: Express server, providers, routing, config API, UI renderers, streams, reasoning, PQC integration.
- [tests/llms.txt](tests/llms.txt) — MJS test contracts, integration fixtures, behavior boundaries.
- [scripts/llms.txt](scripts/llms.txt) — CI/CD and research scripts (MTS/MJS), model validation, catalog aggregation, CIP apply.
- [bin/llms.txt](bin/llms.txt) — Runtime entry points and CLI commands for local-router and PQC secrets.
- [build/llms.txt](build/llms.txt) — Compiled JS outputs from TypeScript; artifact boundary for production deploy.
- [community/llms.txt](community/llms.txt) — Public-facing contribution and community governance docs.
- [data/llms.txt](data/llms.txt) — Research manifests, CIP reports, benchmark sources, model catalog deltas, provider watch data.
- [.agents/llms.txt](.agents/llms.txt) — Operator task files, agent skills, research snapshots.
